name: Potlatch & Gift Economy Systems
summary: Reciprocal gift-giving ceremonies that redistribute wealth, establish social bonds, and maintain balance between communities.

claims.statement: Gift economies prevent wealth concentration and maintain social cohesion across extended kinship networks
Potlatch-type ceremonies have independently arisen in multiple cultures as a wealth redistribution mechanism

evidence.source: Mauss (1925) The Gift: Forms and Functions of Exchange in Archaic Societies
Boas (1966) Kwakiutl Ethnography — potlatch ceremony descriptions
Sahlins (1972) Stone Age Economics — comparative gift economy analysis

notes: Banned by Canadian government 1885-1951; survival despite criminalization demonstrates resilience. Modern parallels in open-source software.
